title: Align Helm chart offline packaging outputs (tarballs + checksums) with signed bundle manifest
creator: Dylan Brooks
content:
Background / why
Air-gapped customers install Redwood Private from an offline bundle. As part of the “signed offline bundles” initiative, the offline bundle manifest will be signed and will include hashes for all included artifacts.

Today, the Helm chart packaging outputs are not consistent across release tooling (naming, output location, checksums), which makes it error-prone to:
- include chart tarballs in the offline bundle reliably
- generate deterministic sha256s that match what the installer verifies
- reference those artifacts from the signed bundle manifest

This ticket coordinates the helm-charts packaging output format with the bundle manifest expectations and release pipeline.

Goals
1) Produce deterministic, machine-consumable Helm chart tarballs for offline bundles.
2) Produce stable checksum outputs for each tarball (sha256) that the bundle generator can ingest.
3) Ensure version alignment between chart version/appVersion and Private bundle version metadata (and build ID annotations as needed for support).

Non-goals
- Redesigning chart contents or values schema (handled separately; see chart validation ticket/PR).
- Introducing new signing primitives inside charts themselves (chart tarballs will be covered by bundle manifest hashing + signature).

Requirements
- Output artifacts MUST be stable across rebuilds of the same git commit (where feasible): tarball contents/order/timestamps should not cause spurious hash changes.
- Checksums MUST use SHA-256 and be emitted in a predictable filename.
- Packaging step MUST run in release CI and produce artifacts consumable by the offline bundle builder.
- Must support multiple charts in repo (redwood-control-plane, redwood-data-plane, optional add-ons).
- Naming convention must be unambiguous and versioned.

Proposed conventions (agreed)
Chart tarball naming:
- <chartName>-<chartVersion>.tgz (Helm standard)

Output directory for release packaging (artifact staging):
- dist/charts/
  - redwood-private-<chartVersion>.tgz
  - redwood-private-<chartVersion>.tgz.sha256
  - redwood-private-<chartVersion>.tgz.prov (optional; not used for verification in Phase 1)

Checksum file format:
- Single-line: "<sha256>  <filename>" (GNU coreutils sha256sum compatible)
- Must be generated from the final .tgz bytes placed into dist/charts/.

Manifest integration expectations
- Offline bundle manifest will include entries for each chart tarball:
  - relative_path: charts/<chartName>-<chartVersion>.tgz
  - sha256: <hex>
  - content_type: application/vnd.cncf.helm.chart
  - version: <chartVersion>
- Bundle builder will copy dist/charts/* into bundleRoot/charts/ and will compute/verify sha256 matches the signed manifest.

Determinism notes
- Helm package can embed timestamps; to reduce rebuild drift we will:
  - ensure packaging runs in a pinned container image and pinned Helm version
  - use SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH when supported by our packaging flow
  - avoid including generated files in charts that have non-deterministic content

Implementation tasks
- [x] Add chart packaging target in redwood-helm-charts release workflow that produces dist/charts/*.tgz.
- [x] Generate sha256 files alongside each tarball in a consistent format.
- [x] Align chart version/appVersion with Private bundle manifest versioning rules.
- [x] Add optional annotations/labels for bundle build ID correlation for Support.
- [x] Document expected outputs for bundle builder + release engineering.

Acceptance criteria
- Given a successful release build, CI publishes dist/charts/*.tgz and corresponding *.sha256 files.
- Offline bundle build can ingest these files without ad-hoc renaming.
- Signed manifest includes chart tarball entries and installer verification passes in air-gapped mode.
- Re-running packaging for the same commit (same toolchain) does not change tarball hash (or drift is documented with a mitigation plan).

References / links
- GitHub: redwood-helm-charts PR-18302 (publish offline chart tarballs with checksums)
- GitHub: redwood-helm-charts PR-18319 (align chart versions with private bundle manifest)
- GitHub: redwood-helm-charts PR-18335 (annotations for bundle build id)
- Confluence: Offline bundle format + manifest (eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging)
- Linear: ENG-4821 (manifest schema + canonicalization)
- Linear: ENG-4822 (pipeline signing step with protected keys)

Testing plan
- CI: add a job that packages charts, computes sha256, and verifies the sha256 file matches the actual tarball.
- Bundle build integration: nightly/RC pipeline builds an offline bundle and runs installer preflight verify on the produced bundle.
- Determinism check: run packaging twice in the same build image and assert identical sha256 for chart artifacts; if drift occurs, capture and file follow-up with root cause (timestamps, file ordering, etc.).

Rollout plan
- Land changes behind the existing release pipeline for Private RC builds.
- Validate in staging air-gapped install (installer preflight verify + actual helm install from local chart tarballs).
- Document the output contract for Release Eng + bundle builder tooling.

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should we rely on Helm provenance (.prov)?
  - A: Not for Phase 1. Integrity is enforced via signed offline bundle manifest hashing. We may add provenance later as additional defense-in-depth but it won’t be required for install.
- Q: Where should checksums live: alongside tarball or aggregated file?
  - A: Alongside each tarball (per-file .sha256) to reduce parsing complexity and match manifest ingestion.

Follow-ups
- If customers request it, consider publishing an aggregated checksums.txt for human validation, but keep per-file .sha256 as the canonical machine input.
- If determinism drift persists across environments, consider switching packaging to a fully hermetic build step (pinned image + explicit env normalization) and document supported toolchain versions.
